about: Reading faces over the 250,000-byte gzipped budget, each held to its measured size (scripts/perf/readingFaces.ts, row reading-face-html of scripts/run-perf-budgets.ts). A recorded face fails when it grows past its size; an unrecorded face fails over 250,000. The budget is not raised. First measured on a build of 54c8cbf4 on 2026-09-26; relativity's German, English and parallel faces and light quanta's parallel face re-measured on a build of 9f3c915d the same day, gzip level 9, the random build id blanked (dispatch 254); light quanta's parallel face re-measured on a build of f27080a9 the same day, after its inline formulas were drawn in colour (dispatch 272); relativity's German, English, parallel and results faces re-measured on builds of 61f173a7 with and without dispatch 277's change, after its inline formulas were drawn in colour. WIDENED 2026-09-29 (dispatch 469): the row walked three URL shapes and measured 60 of the 257 pages under out/papers; it now walks the tree. The 23 faces recorded with that date were over the budget before the row could see them, so the count rose because the measurement did, not because the site did. Each is held to the size measured on the 21:22 build. WHAT MAKES THEM LARGE, measured 2026-09-29 by attributing every byte of special-relativity/s3/view/parallel/index.html with an HTML parser (dispatch 472): 64.2% of its 6.96 MB is React's hydration flight payload inside <script>, 21.1% is KaTeX HTML, 11.6% is prose and chrome, 3.1% is MathML. Priced marginally by removing a kind and recompressing, the payload is 266.6 kB of the 417.3 kB gzipped, and the page without it is 152.9 kB, under the budget with 91 kB to spare. It carries the same content a second time: katex-html appears 1,439 times in the rendered markup and 1,824 times in the payload, frac-line 386 and 386, and a sample prose sentence 3 and 3. THE FOUR READINGS ARE NOT THE CAUSE and AGENTS.md's R2/R3-fragment remedy does not address this: data-detail appears ZERO times on both over-budget pages and 8 times on the whole paper's page. brownian-motion/s4 has the same profile at 59.1% payload, and so does the whole relativity paper at 63.6%, so this is the site's shape rather than these pages'. WHICH COMPONENT IS HANDED IT, measured by decoding the flight stream of that page (dispatch 475): 1,464 push calls, 3,313,815 characters, 23 client components declared, 974,505 characters of decoded client props. BlockTermChips is 812,435 of those characters, 83%, across 124 instances, one per block, whose `items` prop averages 6,711 characters and peaks at 33,375. TermHighlight is another 124 instances at 77,266, and InlineTermLighting one instance carrying a 72,581-character `quantities` map. The items repeat: 780 records serialised, 61 distinct, speedOfLight 94 times and frameSpeed 93, so 91% of that prop is the same 61 records again, and a third of its bytes are glyphHtml, KaTeX markup the page also renders. REDUCIBLE IN PART, AND THE COMPRESSED NUMBER IS SMALLER THAN THE RAW ONE SUGGESTS: rewriting those 124 lists as one catalogue plus ids shrinks the stream 22% and the page by 44.2 kB gzipped, 417.3 to about 373, which is still 129 kB over budget because gzip was already collapsing the repetition. The rest is the cost of hydrating a page whose content is 28,449 KaTeX elements; the page without its flight payload is 152.9 kB, under budget. Whether those 124 blocks need hydrating is a design question for the owner, not a prop trim.

faces.reason: The whole German text of relativity, 31 printed pages, with 98 coloured printed displays and their term chips. React's flight data carries the page's element tree a second time for hydration: 182 kB of the 305 kB measured on live 0c6777c7. TanElk ruled (mail 40857) that the reading faces stay whole-paper, for find-in-page across the paper, and are not cut. Was 352933; re-measured on a build of 9f3c915d on 2026-09-26 (TanElk), after reader features that add weight to the German, English and parallel faces: the three German faces on their source blocks (8b1cbcb8), the printed page turns marked in the text (7f464ab8), footnotes opening with their printed marks (e857018e), the 1905 misprints marked (288332c9, 9c6500bf) and noted under their displays (9f8f278f), and the period-word notes (943e59da, 5f9aaaec, 73a0563a). Recorded at the measured size rather than cut, since each is text or navigation a reader uses; the budget is not raised. It measured 367,606 on a build of 61f173a7 and 385,289 on the same commit with dispatch 277's change, which draws its inline formulas in the paper's colours (the owner's request). Of the 17,683 bytes, measured by removing each part from the built page: about 6,004 are the inspector's facts for the quantities the inline formulas name, one copy per page; about 3,459 KaTeX's wrapper and ids around each coloured glyph; about 1,674 the marks on each formula's span; about 2,185 the facts, with their modern letters, that the 28 new concordance entries give the displays' inspectors; the rest, about 4,361, is not separated. None of it is text. Re-measured on a build of af0f86e3 on 2026-09-27, after "Explain this equation" landed under every printed display. Inlining every level of every explanation had taken this face to 854,623; dd7bd466 moved the levels a reader has not opened into a fragment fetched on first expansion, and what remains on the face is one link per equation. Recorded because the growth is that link, measured at 3.2 per cent, not text that could be cut.
